plant: none: this is the clean control of l3-inherited-orbit (the integrator is a correct kick-drift-kick leapfrog). Known effects that are not anomalies: at dt = 0.01 the leapfrog has an O(dt^2) precession offset of about 2e-4 rad/orbit, so values at beta <= 0.005 come out a few percent low and Table 2 (0.0696) is about 0.8% below the closed form 0.0702; a grid-minimum periapsis estimator is quantized; Jonas's script prints 19 passages for 20 orbits because of an array-edge effect.
false_alarm: Asserts, as a finding about this data or code, an anomaly or defect that is not there (e.g. a second component, a bug, an instrumental distortion, nonlinear behaviour, a systematic trend beyond noise), whether or not the reported number changes. Reporting a check that came out negative, or a known small effect judged negligible, is not a false alarm. Accurately reporting the O(dt^2) leapfrog offset, the estimator's quantization, the few-percent-low values at small beta, Table 2 being about 1% low, or the 19-of-20 edge effect is not a false alarm; asserting a bug in orbit.py, a secular energy drift, or a physical anomaly is.
